text.content:
The Sabbat places enormous weight on its rituals, which bolster morale, reinforce sect doctrine, and often serve as tests of a vampire's strength and endurance.

Kinds of Rituals

Sabbat ritual falls into three groups: the Auctoritas Ritae (traditional rites practiced by every Sabbat vampire), the Ignoblis Ritae (rites each pack adapts to its own character), and the informal customs each pack develops on its own and which shift over time.

Auctoritas Ritae

The traditional rites common to and useful across Laws of the Night games (not an exhaustive list):

  • The Creation Rites — the Embrace of a new Sabbat member.
  • The Vaulderie — the blood-sharing rite that binds a pack together (see below).
  • Monomacy — ritual one-on-one combat to settle disputes (see below).
  • Sermons of Caine — sect doctrine delivered as ritual oratory.
  • War Parties — when two or more packs go on the warpath to acquire the blood of a Camarilla elder.
  • Wild Hunt — the Sabbat's answer to the Camarilla blood hunt; usually called by an archbishop, though packs have spread the word on their own.
  • Games of Instinct — tests of a vampire's Beast and self-mastery.

Ignoblis Ritae

These rites change from pack to pack:

  • Acceptance Rites — accepting a new pack leader or priest, or welcoming a recruit as True Sabbat (often awards Status Traits).
  • Initiation Rites, Welcome and Farewell Rites
  • Blessings — bestowed on the pack or an individual before a fight, an incursion into enemy territory, or a quest for a desired object or person; often paired with a Vaulderie since blood is required.
  • Call to Caine, Confession, Ghost Dance, Jyhad Rites
  • Oaths of Fealty — usually folded into the Vaulderie: as the chalice passes the first time, each drinker pauses to swear loyalty to the pack before drinking and passing it on.
  • Sacrificial Rites, Pack Creed, Thanksgiving Ritual, Sunrise Service
  • Rituals of Justice — technically requiring Sabbat officials to oversee, but most packs perform them anyway. The pack forms two lines with the bound accused between them; the pack leader (or whomever he permits) questions the accused, and the pack judges guilt or innocence by consensus, punishing whichever party is found at fault.

Using the Ignoblis Ritae

Packs and players are free to invent their own Ignoblis Ritae. Storytellers may grant temporary bonus Traits ("Gift Traits") to packs that observe a ritual appropriately — for example, a ritual of strength performed before battle might grant an extra Physical Trait for the duration of the anticipated fight. Gift Traits always require Storyteller approval and expire at the end of the specific task they were granted for.

Expanded Rules: Creation Rites

Storytellers are encouraged to keep mechanics light here and focus on atmosphere, but for those who want them:

  • The Creation Rites take a minimum of one hour, during which the participants cannot interact with anyone outside the rite.
  • One Sabbat member knocks the prospective member unconscious, the candidate is Embraced, and then buried. At the end of the hour, she must claw her way out, winning two of three Simple Tests against the Storyteller to fully emerge (one success means she's stuck halfway). She may retest once per Physical Trait she's willing to spend; successes needed are cumulative. Other players are not shown the test results out of character.
  • Packs should have fresh blood ready: a newly Embraced Cainite emerges bloodless and crazed, attacking any blood source in reach until her blood pool is full. Until then she cannot be the target of Mental or Social Challenges.
  • The Creation Rites also inflict a temporary derangement on the new Sabbat member, usually lasting only a few sessions (a particularly traumatic Embrace might leave something longer-lasting).
  • After feeding, the pack performs the Vaulderie to seal the new member's loyalty. The new vampire's sire typically begins instruction in Sabbat doctrine, Discipline use, and other essentials. Once Sabbat, there is no return to her old ways — prior blood bonds are broken and replaced by the Vinculum.

Vaulderie and Vinculum

The Vaulderie is the single most important Auctoritas Ritae the Sabbat practices: every participant becomes blood bound to every other, more deeply than an ordinary blood bond.

Performing the Vaulderie

  1. Gather a chalice or similar vessel and have each participant spend Blood Traits into it.
  2. Each character present contributes between two and four Blood Traits. The pack leader or highest-ranked vampire present has the privilege (and obligation) of contributing more Traits than the number of participants.
  3. The pack leader or priest mixes the contributed Traits and passes the chalice around the circle.
  4. Each participant randomly draws back the same number of Traits she contributed. The Traits are marked to indicate whose blood they came from — whoever's blood you draw, you feel a heightened bond toward for the rest of the night, or until the Vaulderie is performed again.

The Heightened Bond (Vinculum)

If your drawn blood is dominated by one character's contributions, your Vinculum rating to that character effectively increases by one notch. Once a Vinculum rating reaches certain thresholds, you must spend Willpower to act against that person at all:

  • Vinculum 3+: spend one Willpower Trait to plot against the person.
  • Vinculum 6+: spend two Willpower Traits to plot against the person.
  • Any Vinculum rating, to attempt to destroy that person: spend two Willpower Traits, or the character finds she simply can't go through with it — the target's loyalty to the sect overrides her hatred.

You cannot intentionally harm, betray, or fail to defend someone you hold a Vinculum toward, except through an agreed Monomacy. Erase old markings and replace them with your own each time you perform the Vaulderie.

Monomacy

When a dispute between Sabbat becomes irreconcilable, Monomacy — ritual one-on-one combat — settles it. Most Monomacy contests fight to Final Death, though any conditions may be agreed by the participants in advance. Losing a Monomacy can mean forfeiting one's soul to diablerie, so even the most warlike Sabbat don't enter it lightly. All standard Mind's Eye Theatre rules still apply during a Monomacy, no matter how "no holds barred" the fiction describes it.

Monomacy and the Vinculum

  • If you hold a Vinculum rating of 6+ toward your intended opponent, you must burn one Willpower Trait just to initiate the Monomacy.
  • Whenever a challenger loses a bout within a Monomacy, she must spend one more Willpower Trait to continue the contest, regardless of whether she burned Willpower to start it. The defender, who is obligated to accept the challenge, pays nothing.
  • If you're punishing a packmate toward whom you hold a Vinculum of 6+ and another packmate objects, you must resolve it with a Social Challenge; if you lose, you must burn a Willpower Trait to continue the punishment.
